paragraphs.source_en: Hearing Hatchan's wailing, my master flew into a rage from the crack of dawn and suddenly sat bolt upright on his bedding. At this point, spiritual cultivation, Yagi Dokusen, and everything of the sort had been flung clean beyond the clouds. As he sat up, he scratched all over his head with both hands, scrape, scrape, scrape, almost enough to peel the skin from his scalp. The dandruff that had been piling up for more than a month now flew without the slightest restraint onto the nape of his neck and the collar of his nightclothes. It was a spectacle of truly imposing grandeur. I then looked to see whether my master's mustache had altered its shape; I should have left well enough alone, for the sight gave me a start: it had become a hopeless tangle, bristling every which way. Perhaps the mustache, too, felt that since its owner was plainly angry, it would be improper for it alone to stand there unconcerned; so each hair flew into a rage and charged ahead with violent force in whatever direction it pleased. This, too, was a sight well worth seeing. Yesterday, because it had to face the mirror, those whiskers had obediently lined up in imitation of His Majesty the German Emperor; but after a night's sleep, discipline, grooming, and all the rest were useless, and they at once returned to their original nature, each recovering its own point of departure. It was exactly like my master's overnight spiritual discipline, which by the next day had been wiped away clean, immediately exposing in full his inborn bullheaded nature. That my master, with such an unruly mustache and so violent a disposition, has somehow not been dismissed even now and still manages to serve as a teacher is astonishing. Thinking of this, I understood for the first time how large Japan is; precisely because it is large, I suppose Kaneda and Kaneda's dogs can pass in society as human beings. So long as they can pass as human beings, my master too seems convinced there is no reason he should be dismissed. If the matter ever comes to that, one need only send a postcard to Sugamo Mental Hospital and inquire of Mr. Tendo Kohei; the truth will be understood at once.
